name: US jobless claims
summary: US initial jobless claims 189,000 in the week to 21 Nov; 4-week average 196,000, near its 52-week low
state: Initial US jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 21 Nov, with the four-week average at 196,000, about 0.4% above its 52-week low of 195,250 (FRED). That is far below the 15% Watch line, so this measure shows no sign of rising layoffs as of 26 Nov.
for_you: Layoffs remain low in the US, so job security for most workers is not under unusual pressure by this measure.
why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
